notes: Separate: photography words (JPEG, mugshot, passport photo do not read as art); famous paintings, famous operas (Carmen, Norma, Faust, Salome), film directors, classic film stars, bollywood stars, authors (named things/people under a generic parent); award words (trophy, medal, podium, ribbon read as sport, not film and tv); film festivals (Cannes, Venice, Toronto read as cities). Fiction removed: Muppets/Sesame Street and British TV puppet characters; Tolkien, Narnia, Potter, Bond, Dahl, Paddington, Christie, Wodehouse, Hunger Games, Millennium, Reacher, Lecter, Mockingbird, Catcher, 1984 (still US copyright) and Grapes of Wrath characters; Looney Tunes/Merrie Melodies titles. Kept as public domain: Gatsby (PD since 2021), Tarzan (1912 novel), Pinocchio, Sherlock Holmes. Macrons added where Wikipedia/Te Ara use them (tā moko, kōwhaiwhai, tāniko, Kyōgen, shōnen, shōjo, tankōbon, bishōnen, seiyū, chūnibyō, Wētā FX); Noh, Shonen Jump (English edition brand), inro, shodo left plain. Titles with periods use the US form with the British form in uk (Mr. Darcy/Mr Darcy, Dr. Jekyll/Dr Jekyll, Mr. Punch/Mr Punch). Pre-existing: 'theater' (parent) holds venues and playwrights rather than generic words; musicals words lists both 'show tune' and 'showtune'. 'The Great Wave' is a woodblock print, not strictly a painting.
